intro: Section 24.2 covers genetic counseling in psychiatry: who provides it and what it includes, how genes and environment combine in psychiatric disorders (Table 24-2), taking a family history and drawing a pedigree (Figures 24-1 and 24-2), the steps of counseling (Table 24-3), risk communication, psychosocial support, and the challenges and ethics of presymptomatic and susceptibility testing. Update boxes add large genome studies, polygenic scores, APOE testing before anti-amyloid drugs and genetic discrimination law.
objectives: Define genetic counseling and its three elements.
Explain why most psychiatric disorders are complex rather than single-gene.
List what a psychiatric family history should include and the steps of counseling.
Communicate recurrence risk in the way a client prefers.
Describe the psychosocial and ethical issues of presymptomatic and susceptibility testing.
